documentNotes.title: General instructions — Observational Exam
documentNotes.statement:
- The duration of the exam is 20 min for each student.
- There will be a copy of these instructions inside the envelope with the exam that will be given to you.
- The exam is individual, and **no conversation** with anybody except with the guide who will be helping you with the telescope is allowed.
- The necessary sky charts are included in the exam that will be handed to you.
- In questions that involve pointing the telescope, the student can ask help of assistant at any time, at the cost of not getting the full marks for that question.
- **Material provided for each student:** red flashlight, laser pointer, pencil, pen, eraser and clipboard.
- **WRITE YOUR ANSWERS IN INK.** The organization will give you pens.

problems.statement: Use your green laser pointer to aim at the stars Antares ($\alpha$-Sco), Vega ($\alpha$-Lyr), Altair ($\alpha$-) and Peacock ($\alpha$-Pav). Also point to the constellation Corona Australis. (Duration: 3 min)

solution.statement:
**Official key item 5:** Students will have **3 minutes** to complete this task.

**Source note.** The supplied key gives no further pointing-location answer or marking scheme for this task. Its item 5 corresponds to question 1; the other key items are shifted by one.
solution.incompleteReason: The supplied official key provides only the duration for the pointing task; no location diagram or detailed rubric is supplied.

problems.statement: Estimate the diameter of the field of view of this telescope, using 10mm Plössl eyepiece and ***star chart-1***, showing nearby region of open cluster NGC 6231. On ***star chart 1*** there are two angular distances shown. Use them as reference. Express your answer in arc minutes. (Duration: 5 min)

figures.caption: CHART 1 - NGC 6231 Field of view
figures.alt: Star chart (TheSky (c) Astronomy Software 1984-1998) of the field around the open cluster NGC 6231, with the dense cluster near the centre; two hand-drawn lines from one star below the cluster are labelled 13.3' and 9.5'; two bright stars at the bottom are labelled ζ2 and ζ1.

solution.statement:
**Official key item 1:** Telescope already pointed to that region (or not?) (5 minutes).

**Answer: 24,0 arc minutes (0.4°).** We will tolerate up to 10% error as correct answer. Error between 10 to 20% will be considered 70% correct.

problems.statement:
Use ***star chart-2*** to estimate the magnitude of the missing star, shown as a cross, inside NGC 6231. Use magnitude of other stars as reference.

**Note**: To avoid confusion between decimal dot and real stars, dots are suppressed. So, magnitude 60 correspond to magnitude 6.0. Give your answer using one decimal scale and 0.1 precession. (Duration: 5 min)

figures.caption: CHART 2 - NGC 6231 – Star magnitudes
figures.alt: Star chart of the open cluster NGC 6231 with a cross marking the missing star; several reference stars are labelled in red with magnitudes without decimal point: 55, 80, 89, 89, 88 and 65.

solution.statement: **Official key item 2:** Exact answer is **magnitude 7.9**, but values between **7.7–8.1** are assumed correct (0.2 magnitude tolerance). Values between **7.5–7.7** or **8.1–8.3** will be considered as **70% correct**. (5 minutes)

problems.statement: Point your telescope to the binary star **$\varepsilon$ Trianguli Australis** using ***star chart-3*** as guide. If you are not able to point at the star, the instructor will do it for you but you lose 50% of the points. That pair components are magnitude 4.1 and 9.3 separated by 82”. Evaluate color of each star: (Duration: 2 min pointing, 3 min determining the color)

figures.caption: CHART 3 - ε Trianguli Australis location
figures.alt: Star chart (TheSky (c) Astronomy Software 1984-1998) of the southern sky with constellation lines and boundaries of Circinus, Triangulum Australis, Crux, Musca, Apus, Chamaeleon and Octans, stars labelled with Greek letters; a hand-drawn blue arrow points to ε in Triangulum Australis.

solution.statement:
**Official key item 3:** (5 minutes)

| Component | White/blue | Yellow | Red | Spectral type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Brighter | | X | | K0III |
| Dimmer | X | | | B9IV |

If the student is not able to point to the star the evaluator will do so, but student loses half of the points.

**Alternate source note.** The text edition allocates 3 minutes to pointing and 2 minutes to evaluating color; the main question sheet prints 2 and 3 minutes respectively.

problems.statement: Individual telescopes will be pointed to some objects. Identify wich one correspond to: Open Cluster **(OC)**, Globular Cluster **(GC)**, Emission Nebulae **(EN)** and Planetary Nebulae **(PN)**. (Duration: 2 minutes, 30’ per object)

solution.statement:
**Official key item 4:** Targets pointed by the evaluator will be M22, M8, M7 and M57. Student will have **30 seconds** to evaluate each target.

| Object | Target | Classification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | M22 | GC |
| 2 | M57 | PN |
| 3 | M7 | OC |
| 4 | M8 | EN |
